Ford v Ferrari is essentially a $100 million superhero movie where the capes are made of grease and Italian leather. The roar of the GT40 and the kinetic chemistry between Damon and Bale is cliche.  I wanted some depth, but I found myself idling. Between the cartoonishly evil corporate villains and a family subplot that feels like it was written by an algorithm, the film frequently veers into by-the-numbers territory. It’s a stalled ride.

Weak dialogues coupled with bad storytelling made this quite forgettable. Really the only reason to watch this is for car noises and period set design. Notevole la quasi completa assimilazione di Henry Ford II in un vero e proprio decerebrato che trascorre la maggior parte delle sue scene a bocca aperta come un pirla mentre gli spiegano le robe, caratterizzazione contrastata dalla sua unica capacità tangibile di fare discorsi accattivanti incazzato nero, momenti di lucidità rari e sporadici, che lo rende paurosamente vicino ad un altro gigante dell’imprenditoria, il sinestetico Claudio Lotito ( per non parlare della scena in cui si cagaspiscia addosso e si mette a piangere dopo un giro di prova). Per il resto, Matt Damon interpreta Matt Damon negli anni ’60 e dispiace per Christian Bale, che, dopo aver guidato per quelle che sembrano 68 ore a Le Mans l’unica macchina al mondo che non esplode superati i 10.000 giri (negli anni ’60), mentre la Ferrari del suo rivale sembrava un decespugliatore dai rumori che faceva, e dopo aver vinto la gara della sua vita, decide di esplodere ridendo a 7.000 giri, su un circuito del cazzo e completamente deserto.

Honestly, I was expected something better. Damon and Bale are great, but the Ford true story angle just played out dry and trite and uninteresting. The music, even though I've liked Beltrami's work in the past, was subpar and didn't add to the emotion of the film. A lot of the time it watched like a true-story-play-by-numbers script. Can't say I'd recommend, even though it's not a bad film. Just pretty forgettable honestly.

Beautiful-looking, spoonfed bullshit. Well, beautiful sounding too. There were only two women characters in the film, and the only one given any dimension whatsoever was the car. Beyond the cartoonishly bad woman-as-wife portrayal, the other characters all fell under equally cartoonish good and evil dynamics. It's a shame that so much good editing, cinematography, sound design, and an unsurprisingly satisfying performance from Christian Bale, was packaged into this predictable, shallow, and unsatisfying movie. I caught this film whilst staying at a hotel so maybe it wasn't the best condition to absorb the film in its fullest intention, but I felt it was the most mid film I've potentially ever seen. I don't think I've ever begged a film more to do something interesting in my life, and it wasnt necessarily a bad film or poorly shot or acted - it was fine - but I felt my brain mushing to an unfocused sludge as it just did absolutely nothing for me. Maybe if I liked cars, racing cars, men talking about cars, or I was just one of Those Dads that you see taking a picture of A Car parked in the street because look at the shiny-shiny then maybe I'd have felt something other than an existential numbness whilst watching this film. Okay I'm being deliberately dramatic but it's a long and flat film other than vroom vroom that didn't boom boom.

“Giddy-up! Giddy-up!” Yes, he says that. I swear on my life. Go ahead—watch this 2h 30m movie to try and prove me wrong. He actually says it FIVE times WHY is Christian Bale in EVERYTHING? This is not the kind of actor I usually consider to be “in everything,” and he certainly isn’t in ME, but here he is—voice of Howl, Batman for some mf reason, The Bride—I just Googled it, WHERE is he in LITTLE WOMEN???? SHAFT?????? NEWSIES??????? He lowkey pulls a Zendaya here. Like, good job, Chrissy (I DO know him like that), but you’re still Christian Bale and you are Patrick Bateman and that’s about it. Wrap it up. I mean, he’s good, really good, but him being British here ticks me off. Okay, I came out swinging and I have to say that I WANTED TO LIKE this movie!! It took me a second, but I realized I was actually pretty entertained despite being critical of pretty much everything while I was watching it. Like, I was WATCHING CARS on a SCREEN. I was gonna give it a 3 or a 3.5. What kind of sad chick am I that I’m saying “I like this movie! THREE!”? Ignore. But anyway, I was gonna give it that rating because, y’know, there were a couple really pretty shots, but the cinematography TO ME was eh, and also…the characters are lowkey buns. I thought this even before the Great Rating Drop of 2026. The longer we went through the movie, the more I saw distinct personalities, so THAT was good. But, y’know, the ONE female character was horrid. Mollie? Bro, the most “woman written by a man” character ever. “I know you’re covered in oil, but I’m in a pretty dress—you want to crack open a beer and dance and play some music?” To quote my buddy Alex, “Get the hell out.” To quote me complaining about this movie to my buddy Cam (I’m committing so many sins by not indenting per quote, I’m sorry to all the kids whose homework I did on IXL in seventh grade), “I don’t care if my man’s covered in oil, that’s kinda hot, but I feel like that’s not the average POV.” It’s giving male fantasy, it’s giving beer ad, and I’m the woker for this and I DO NOT CARE! Mollie has a whole scene where she’s leaning against the doorway while Ken (CBale) is talking to his son before bed, and she’s looking all longingly…WHAT ARE WE DOING? Oh my God, or when CBale and Matt Damon’s characters are getting into a tussle, and she’s like “Are you boys done fighting😉?” And one of them is GENUINELY like “get me a soda? [🇬🇧]” and she’s all “okaaaaay~! <3” ?????? ?? ???? Dog what is this. ALSO she has this moment when she’s like “I don’t want you to go out there driving again!! It’s dangerous!!” Son SHUT UP I’ve SEEN this movie with buttcheeks gulag (The Courier) and it STILL PMO. GET JESSIE BUCKLEY IN HERE🗣️🗣️!! Jessie Buckley? Christian Bale? Is this Cine2Nerdle, because that’s The Bride! Wow! I’m still mad, you can’t distract me. Anyway, I was still gonna give it a three. But. Okay, it feels like I watched a Moviedle of a different movie at the end. A different movie? A different review? I still have to write, like, twelve. Whatever. Here. New quote! “My main goal is to blow up and act like I don’t know nobody.” This ending PISSED ME OFF!! It has been over a MONTH and I STILL REMEMBER!! Spoiler warning? No shit. But this is actually a pretty big twist (because it makes no sense) so if you ever want to watch it and fully get the experience, you should have stopped reading a minute ago, because your peripheral vision is probably already picking up the spoiler. I am STILL mad, you STILL cannot distract me STILL. Okay, not the twist, but if you’ve seen this movie, you know what I was alluding to a second ago. Let’s start here: Christian Bale has shown NO indication—yes, he drives for the love of the game, the money’s cool, but it’s not about the money—that he would EVER slow down. WHYYYY would he slow down? And then the loss makes you feel awful, because you just watched a 2.5 hour movie to see them lose. “Maybe that was the point.” “That’s how life is.” It’s been a LONG time since I used that quote when talking about a movie that did pretty pointless emo shit! I know it’s based on an actual race, so they’re not going to change the outcome, but you are rewriting a man’s life and you can’t make this make sense SOMEWHERE in those 2.5 hours? And the DEATH was framed like ABSOLUTE dogwater! Anthony and I kept joking “any minute now” and yukking up about characters blowing up, so it was actually crazy when it happened—in fact, I LIKED how it was shot and done! Having it in the last ten minutes makes it even more shocking…but then, y’know, past the shock, what are you going to do in the last ten minutes? If we want to do the dramatic/sad route, end on Bale getting his shit blown smoove off. Don’t make me think I’m gonna get Damon/Mollie on some Vance/Erika shite or…try to fit in some sort of message? It felt weird. That’s all. I sound remarkably mad about a movie I gave two stars, but I was peeved. Was I entertained? Regrettably, absolutely. You win this round.

Swaggering with the bravado of a Jerry Bruckheimer film and boasting a USA #1 mentality, Ford vs Ferrari has fancy editing but never truly makes the heart pound. I believe Matt Damon was miscast for a Tommy Lee Jones-like role and Christian Bale becomes a cartoonish Cockney whose lines are essentially rattling off car parts. The movie feels like a throwback to the blockbusters from 40 years ago (Top Gun, Armageddon, etc.) and delivers the same kind of glossy sheen. But under the hood, there’s just not much depth.
